$comment: The four presence/nullability combinations of FR-066, cell by cell. Every expectation here is read off the table in `spec/functional/FR-066-generate-runtime-validators.md` under `### Presence, nullability, and the four combinations` and off `ir/presence.ir.json`'s own declarations. None was recorded from a run of the generated validator: an expectation minted by the implementation under test is not evidence, which is the discipline `provenance.blessedFromRun` states for the conformance corpus.

cases.title: every field present and conforming is accepted
required and non-nullable: absent is rejected
required and non-nullable: null is rejected
required and nullable: absent is rejected
required and nullable: null is accepted
optional and non-nullable: absent is accepted
optional and non-nullable: null is rejected
optional and nullable: absent is accepted
optional and nullable: null is accepted
a required property present with the value undefined is rejected
cases.differentialReason: JSON has no representation for `undefined`, so a JSON Schema document cannot express the difference between an absent property and one present with `undefined`. FR-066 makes that difference decidable only by an own-property test, which is outside the JSON data model ajv works in.

cases.title: an optional property present with the value undefined is rejected
cases.differentialReason: As PRES-010: `undefined` is not a JSON value, so the second decider cannot see the case at all.

cases.title: an inherited member does not satisfy a declared field
cases.differentialReason: A prototype chain is not part of the JSON data model. ajv validates the object's enumerable own and inherited members alike through ordinary property access, so it cannot distinguish the two; FR-066 requires an own-property test.

cases.title: an accessor member is not read and is reported rather than invoked
cases.differentialReason: A getter is not a JSON value. ajv reads the property, invoking the getter, so the second decider would throw where FR-066 requires the first to report.

cases.title: an object with a null prototype validates identically
a value that is not an object is rejected at the root pointer
an array is not a record
null is not a record
a nullable collection field accepts null for the collection itself
a nullable collection field does not admit a null member
an absent nullable collection is accepted
a collection member of the wrong type is rejected at its index
